blockedIdentities.reason: ARTEC is used by multiple unrelated active manufacturers, including industrial-valve, three-dimensional scanning and vehicle-component businesses. The queue record has no legal-name, country or product-scope discriminator that safely selects one manufacturer-owned source.
ARTEN does not resolve to a unique industrial manufacturer. Several unrelated companies and product brands use the name, and the repository record provides no reliable identity discriminator.
ASAHI is shared by multiple unrelated industrial manufacturers and corporate groups. The raw name alone cannot safely distinguish the intended valve, bearing, glass or other industrial entity.
ASK is a generic three-letter name used by unrelated motion-control, bearing, electronics and automotive businesses. No queue-level discriminator safely identifies one manufacturer-owned domain.
ASM is used by multiple unrelated manufacturers, including ASM Sensors and ASM International. The undifferentiated queue identity cannot be assigned to one of them without guessing.

Historical reseller material associates ATAV with electric motors, but no current manufacturer-owned or explicit official-parent source was found that establishes the legal or commercial identity. Reseller evidence is not sufficient for BRAND_SAFE.

ATMOS is used by several unrelated active manufacturers. A Czech compressor maker is a plausible match, but the raw identity has no country or product-scope discriminator that excludes the other ATMOS entities.

ATS is a generic abbreviation shared by multiple unrelated automation, thermal-management, testing and manufacturing companies. The repository identity cannot be resolved safely to one manufacturer-owned source.

AUTOMATIONSTECHNIK is a generic German descriptor used in many unrelated company names. The queue record supplies no legal name, location or product scope that can establish a unique manufacturer identity.
AXOR is an active name in unrelated industrial-drive and sanitary-product businesses. The raw queue record does not provide enough context to choose one official identity safely.
BACHMANN is shared by unrelated industrial-automation, electrical-component and other manufacturers. The numeric repository suffix is not an evidence-backed identity discriminator.

The official Bachofen site verifies a Swiss industrial-automation engineering, distribution and service company, but it presents a portfolio of partner products rather than a distinct manufacturer-owned product line. That evidence does not satisfy the manufacturer identity gate.
BAE is a generic abbreviation and can refer to multiple unrelated corporate and product identities. The queue record contains no legal-name, country or product-scope discriminator.

Official evidence resolves STEVI to a product family of ARI-Armaturen, which is already represented by the canonical ari-armaturen manufacturer profile. A second manufacturer page would duplicate the same legal identity.

ACOPOS is an official B&R motion-control product family, while B&R Industrial Automation is already represented by the canonical br-automation manufacturer profile. It is not a separate manufacturer identity.
